Thomas Jefferson in a letter to William Torrance wrote: “The…question, whether the judges are invested with exclusive authority to decide on the constitutionality of a law, has been heretofore a subject of consideration with me in the exercise of official duties. Certainly there is not a word in the Constitution which has given that power to them more than to the executive or legislative branches.”

The idea that courts have an exclusive right to declare laws unconstitutional comes from a misreading of Marbury v. Madison. Marbury stands for the proposition that the Constitution binds every branch of government, and each branch must follow it. Marbury should not be read to authorize judicial supremacy.

Updated Debt Repayment
Projected U.S. Population Increase: From 341 million in 2024 to ~412 million by 2065 (0.3% annual growth).

Projected Inflation Increase: 2% annually, compounding to ~120% over 40 years (PCE price index).

Projected Debt Increase: From $36 trillion in 2025 to ~$75 trillion by 2065 (118% to 156% of GDP).

Average Taxpayer Income: $59,228 in 2024, rising to ~$242,000 by 2065 (3.5% nominal growth).

Time and % Income Tax to Repay $36 Trillion:
To repay $36 trillion (adjusted to $79.5 trillion in 2065 dollars) over 40 years, income taxes must increase by ~22% (from 14% to 17.07% effective rate), generating $1.99 trillion annually.

Alternatively, dedicating 10% of each taxpayer’s income (~$24,200 in 2065) solely to debt repayment would take ~12.3 years, but this is impractical as it ignores other federal obligations and ongoing deficits.

Feasibility: Repaying $36 trillion within a worker’s lifetime is highly unlikely due to rising debt, interest costs, and economic constraints. A balanced approach (tax increases, spending cuts) would be needed, but current projections suggest fiscal unsustainability within 20 years.
